observation: Plasma protein-affinity / pQTL associations nominate MANSC4.
evidence_details: Plasma proteomic/pQTL studies associate the assay labelled MANSC4 with type-1 diabetes outcomes and, separately, normal-tension glaucoma. The glaucoma study combines UK Biobank Olink protein measurements with several pQTL cohorts and Mendelian-randomization analyses.
interpretation: A plasma affinity signal and genetic association do not localize normal protein to a tissue. Genetic effects can concern protein abundance or assay binding. Verify reagent selectivity and use an orthogonal peptide assay before treating the signal as identified circulating MANSC4 or assigning a producing cell.
next_action: Verify the reagent’s target and the producing tissue; a plasma association is not tissue-localized protein evidence.

observation: Recent work supports a nucleolar long-noncoding-RNA interpretation of the FRG2 family and challenges translation claims.
evidence_details: The 2025 study introduced N- or C-terminal FLAG tags into predicted FRG2-family ORFs in HeLa and HEK293 cells. Tagged transcripts were detected and induced by doxorubicin, but FLAG immunoblots did not detect protein. Ribosome-profile and proteomic searches, including a HeLa experiment detecting more than 6,000 proteins, also found no FRG2 protein. RNA experiments support nucleolar/chromatin functions.
interpretation: This is affirmative experimental counterevidence to a protein interpretation, stronger than simply lacking a paper. The work examines several paralogs and edited bulk cell populations; align its tested transcripts/frames to the selected FRG2 or FRG2B sequence. Failure in those models is not a universal demonstration that no condition produces a protein.
next_action: Review the exact locus and reading frame against the published experiments before retaining a protein-level claim.
